# Can every mature plant cell do this?

## A cell must be alive to divide

Steward used phloem cells, which are alive. To divide, a cell needs its living contents: its cytoplasm and its nucleus. Some permanent tissues are made of dead cells, though. A mature xylem vessel and most sclerenchyma cells are dead, with thick walls made hard by lignin.

## Which cells can start again

- A living cell, such as a phloem cell or a parenchyma cell, can sometimes regain the ability to divide.
- A dead xylem vessel or sclerenchyma fibre has no living contents, so no medium can make it divide.

**Only living plant cells can be totipotent, and even living cells need the right conditions to show it.**
